essential_domain_extension.rationale: The root factorization bundles the revocation event with the enforcement point under enforcement-failure-revocation-and-propagation. Constraint AA-06 requires distinguishing three separable moments: (a) the time the revocation decision is recorded at the policy layer, (b) the stated propagation window to the enforcement point, and (c) the enforcement point's actual invalidation of the cached decision. Without a separately trackable field for this lifecycle sequence, an audit cannot determine whether a stale-grant access event occurred within or outside the stated propagation contract. This is the direct cause of the structured failure below and is not detectable from the bundled factor alone.
essential_domain_extension.basis: coder proposal; derived from constraint AA-06, the entry contrast row decision vs. enforcement, and the constraint view failure sign: cached decisions have no invalidation contract
essential_domain_extension.scope: minimal: add as a named sub-record or optional extension field under enforcement-failure-revocation-and-propagation; does not require restructuring the primary factorization

structured_failure.condition: An entitlement has been revoked at the policy layer, but the enforcement point holds a cached authorization decision issued before the revocation was propagated. The propagation window for the revocation event is not tracked as a distinct record. The enforcement point cannot distinguish a valid cached decision from a stale post-revocation decision because revocation time, propagation window, and enforcement-point invalidation time are stored in the same bundled field.
structured_failure.consequence: The subject retains access after entitlement revocation for an indeterminate period. The audit record cannot reconstruct whether the enforcement action was within the stated propagation contract, simultaneously violating AA-06 (stale grant active beyond contract) and AA-02 (decision cannot be reconstructed from the record). The access event is auditably ambiguous: it cannot be classified as authorized, unauthorized, or within propagation tolerance.

generic_property_graph_sufficient.conditions: A generic scoped property graph with named node types for subject, resource, operation, permission, policy-version, entitlement, decision, enforcement-point, and audit-record and directed typed edges for informs, supports, grants, enables, and constrains can represent the primary factorization and the eight constraint invariants. The fail-closed semantics of AA-04 (missing facts become deny, not implicit allow) and the revocation-propagation window of AA-06 require named extension annotations—specifically a propagation-window property on the enforcement-point node and a revocation-event edge type between entitlement and enforcement-point. These are domain extensions, not violations of the graph representation model. The representation is sufficient with those two extensions.

essential_domain_extension.rationale: The root factorization includes temperature-and-pressure-where-volume-matters but does not provide a separately trackable field for the before/after-mixing volume convention (whether component volumes are measured before mixing or refer to a declared post-mixing measurement convention). The entry and formula view both list volume nonadditivity as a failure sign and the formula view requires a four-point declaration for volume fraction, but without a distinct named factor this declaration cannot be tracked at the record level. A downstream record that conflates pre-mixing and post-mixing volumes cannot be detected by a field-level audit of the primary factorization alone.
essential_domain_extension.basis: coder proposal; derived from the volume-fraction scope section of the formula view (four required declarations) and the entry failure sign: before-mixing volumes are equated with final solution volume without a stated model
essential_domain_extension.scope: minimal: add as an optional extension field for any record involving volume-fraction or volume-based concentration; does not restructure the primary factorization

structured_failure.condition: A volume fraction is computed as the ratio of individual component volumes measured before mixing to the final measured post-mixing mixture volume. No volume-convention record exists. The fraction closure condition (sum of volume fractions = 1) is then asserted for this set, treating the before-mixing component volumes as the denominator even though the reported denominator is the final mixture volume.
structured_failure.consequence: The reported volume fractions are internally inconsistent: their numerators (pre-mixing component volumes) and the implied denominator (sum of those same pre-mixing volumes) differ from the denominator actually used (post-mixing mixture volume). The closure claim is false for any solution where volumes are not additive on mixing. Any subsequent composition-basis conversion using these volume fractions propagates a systematic error, and the source of the inconsistency cannot be recovered without the missing volume-convention record.

generic_property_graph_sufficient.conditions: The seven canonical relations form a directed typed graph: entity-count → amount-of-substance (via Avogadro constant), component amount/mass → concentration (via mixture volume), component → fraction (via exhaustive totals), mass/amount → molar mass (bridge property), amount-fraction → mass-fraction (basis transformation via component molar masses). All factors and directed relations can be encoded in a typed property graph. The closure constraint (sum_i(x_i) = 1 for an exhaustive set) cannot be expressed as a binary edge between individual component nodes; it requires either a hyperedge or an aggregate-constraint node over the full component set. The volume-nonadditivity contract similarly requires a declared-volume-convention edge qualifier. A generic property graph with extension for constraint-closure aggregate nodes and declared-volume-convention edge qualifiers is representationally sufficient.

essential_domain_extension.rationale: The root factor candidate-alternatives-and-generation-boundary bundles the alternative instances with the scope of the generation process. There is no separately trackable sub-record for: (a) when the generation process was conducted, (b) who conducted it, (c) what mandate or question framed it, and (d) whether the preferred criterion or expected outcome was known at generation time. Without this, a post-hoc re-generation of alternatives shaped around a preferred option cannot be detected by audit. The feasibility-constraints-and-exclusion-rationale factor records why alternatives were excluded after generation, not how the initial candidate set was scoped before screening. These are distinct and the distinction is required to detect the most consequential generation-bias failure.
essential_domain_extension.basis: coder proposal; derived from the decision view failure sign: Alternatives are generated after the preferred criterion or score is known; and from the second failure sign: Current practice is omitted because the proposed change is already favored
essential_domain_extension.scope: minimal: add as a required sub-record of the candidate-alternatives-and-generation-boundary factor (generation-time, generation-mandate, and known-outcome-at-generation flag); does not require restructuring the primary factorization

structured_failure.condition: The candidate alternative set is constructed after the preferred evaluation criterion or expected outcome is already known. No generation-boundary record exists documenting when alternatives were generated, by whom, or whether the expected outcome was known at that time. The current-practice or no-action alternative is omitted without a documented exclusion rationale, because the proposed alternative is already favored.
structured_failure.consequence: The feasibility stage is corrupted because the comparison cannot be reconstructed from the record: alternatives consistent with the generation bias are over-represented, the omitted baseline cannot be recovered, and the exclusion-rationale field is empty. An independent reviewer cannot separate the analytical record from the pre-shaped generation scope. The recommendation is not falsifiable by review because its foundation—the candidate set—was shaped to produce it.

generic_property_graph_sufficient.conditions: The five f27-family typed relations with their named qualifiers are directly representable as directed typed edges with edge-property maps in a generic property graph. The four-stage structure of the decision view can be encoded as ordered stage-nodes with input and output contracts as node properties. The noncompensatory-gate semantics (a hard constraint cannot be overridden by criterion scores) requires a distinct edge type—feasibility-constraint-gate—that differs from the comparison edges used in Stage 3; this is a domain extension, not a violation of the graph model. The cell-status enum (observed, estimated, missing, contested, not-applicable) requires an edge annotation on the alternative-state-outcome edge. The generation-boundary record proposed as an extension requires a separate provenance-node linked to the alternatives node. With these three extensions (feasibility-constraint-gate edge type, cell-status edge annotation, and generation-boundary provenance node), a generic property graph is representationally sufficient.

terminology_comparison.formography_explanation: The label requires defining seven new technical terms before use: form (organization of factors and relations under a declared frame), factor (selected constituent in one view, not automatically causal or independent), relation (typed, directed, scoped correspondence or dependency), frame (question, purpose, perspective, context, scale, and version), formograph (one bounded inspectable map), projection (loss-declared view for one use), and custody (source path, digest, authority, review state, and unresolved state remain reconstructable). None of these have standard prior definitions outside the protocol; all require the working definitions in the protocol document. Once loaded, the label precisely names, as a single unit, the full method contract: alternative factorizations, typed relations, source custody, boundary declaration, and projection loss. However, the term has a confirmed prior collision with Lippert/Kuehnen/Wagenknecht's 2021 ethnographic formography proposal, which requires an explicit disambiguation statement for academic audiences and adds explanation overhead in that context.
terminology_comparison.governed_property_graph_explanation: The label can be parsed as a property graph—entities with typed properties and directed typed edges, a well-established concept in graph databases, graph theory, and knowledge representation—that is governed: subject to declared authority, version, scope, and constraint. Both components have established technical meanings, making the label immediately parseable by readers familiar with graph databases or knowledge graphs. However, 'governed' in graph-database contexts typically means schema enforcement, access-control policy, or data lineage governance—not epistemological source custody, alternative factorizations, or loss-declared projections. A reader applying the standard graph-database meaning of 'governed' would have an incomplete understanding of the method's contract: they would not infer that the method requires alternative factorizations to remain visible, that projection loss must be declared, or that competing factorizations of the same form are valid and co-present. The label is more accessible but carries a systematic mapping error for the most technically fluent readers.
terminology_comparison.reason: Formography is more precise for the full method contract. For the three cases coded, the decisive distinguishing features of the method—retaining alternative factorizations, declaring projection loss, maintaining source custody as an epistemological rather than a provenance-only requirement, and naming boundaries explicitly—are not communicated by 'governed property graph' even for a reader who fully understands property graphs and governance. The marginal disambiguation cost for 'formography' (loading seven new terms plus one collision disclaimer) is justified by the precision gain: a practitioner who understands the seven terms has the full contract with no systematic mapping error. A practitioner who understands 'governed property graph' in the graph-database sense lacks at least three of the contract's most distinctive features. Confidence is moderated by the genuine accessibility advantage of the alternative label and by the fact that the term collision with TU Dresden formography could predictably mislead an academic audience in STS or sociology.

overall_falsification_assessment: The proposed governed-method-profile thesis—that Formography names a distinct, independently applicable, and falsifiable method for mapping context-bounded forms through alternative factorizations, typed relations, source custody, and loss-declared projections—survives my independent coding in a limited and conditional sense. All three cases (access-authorization, amount-concentration-composition, and choice-alternative-selection) yielded consistent application of the nine required core categories without requiring silent redefinition of any core term. The same frame structure, projection-loss declaration, and structured-failure identification applied across a governance domain, a quantitative science domain, and an evaluative decision domain. Each case produced a distinct and source-backed projection-loss finding (a reader using only the constraint view, formula view, or decision view cannot recover the entry's conceptual orientation or selection procedure) and a consequential structured failure (CLAWS-AA-REVOC-01, CLAWS-ACC-VOLFRAC-01, CLAWS-CAS-GENBOUND-01) that the Formography contract would surface at the field level through the essential domain extension. The thesis does not survive as a claim of representational novelty over generic property graphs. A generic scoped property graph with domain extensions is representationally sufficient for all three cases, consistent with the foundation module's finding. The method's demonstrated value is in the structured naming of factors, boundaries, alternative factorizations, and projection loss—not in requiring a novel storage or graph representation. Four conditions would falsify the thesis: (1) independent coders cannot agree on the canonical form_owner in any case, showing the primary authority concept is not operationally clear; (2) essential domain extensions proposed across coders have no majority-supported overlapping core, showing the method does not produce a stable factorization contract; (3) a standard schema.org property graph with versioning annotations produces equally precise projection-loss records and structured-failure identification for all three cases without the Formography vocabulary, showing the vocabulary adds no explanatory utility; (4) a domain expert using the Formography contract cannot identify a category error that a domain expert using an unstructured description would also identify, showing the method provides no incremental diagnostic value. On current evidence, the thesis survives as a candidate field-level method description that is independently applicable across domains, but remains unestablished as a distinct academic field and unproven as representationally novel beyond governed property graphs with domain extensions.
